key_insight: pUniFind is a single large-scale deep learning model trained on >100 million spectra that unifies peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing, enabling substantially improved peptide identification and discovery of modifications.
problem_solved: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics requires both accurate peptide–spectrum matching and flexible de novo discovery of modifications; existing tools treat these tasks separately and struggle at large scale and for unknown modifications.
method: Train a unified deep learning model on a massive multimodal dataset (spectra paired with peptide sequences and annotation/metadata) to learn joint representations.
Combine peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing in a single framework so the model can both match known peptides and propose novel/modified sequences.
Leverage scale (100M+ spectra) and multimodal inputs to improve robustness to noise, modifications, and diverse instrument conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, pUniFind demonstrates the value of large-scale, multimodal training to merge complementary tasks into one model—improving accuracy and enabling discovery at proteomics scale, while reducing fragmentation of toolchains.
visual_elements: Schematic of the unified model: inputs (mass spectra, metadata) → shared encoder → two heads (scoring head and de novo sequencing head).

paper_title: A large-scale unified deep learning model for peptide mass spectrum interpretation trained on multimodal data
paper_authors: Jiale Zhao, Pengzhi Mao, Kaifei Wang, Yiming Li, Yaping Peng
